title: Deep-learning-enhanced Sparta earthquake catalog resolves a shallow multifault rupture
summary: For the 2020 Mw 5.1 Sparta, North Carolina sequence, an EQTransformer-based catalog combined with matched-filter detections and differential-time relocations contains 1,761 high-precision events, about 5.8 times the original NEIC count. The denser locations resolve several shallow clusters and support the authors’ interpretation that the mainshock nucleated near the intersection of a blind strike-slip fault and a reverse fault associated with the surface rupture; moment-tensor inversion places its centroid at about 1.3 km depth.
ai_technology: Earthquake Transformer (EQTransformer) deep-learning phase/event detector, followed by matched-filter detection and differential-time relocation
organization: Georgia Institute of Technology; University of Science and Technology of China; North Carolina State University; Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: For the 2020 Mw 5.1 Sparta, North Carolina sequence, an EQTransformer-based catalog combined with matched-filter detections and differential-time relocations contains 1,761 high-precision events, about 5.8 times the original NEIC count.
evidence.unknown: This is a retrospective study of one 2020 earthquake sequence, using a local temporary-network deployment. The authors describe the inferred fault intersection/flower-structure interpretation as possible; the fit for the smallest cluster is poor and its geometry uncertain. The result is not a forecast or general fault model. The AI contribution was event detection within a hybrid workflow, not independent geological validation.
evidence.ai_role: EQTransformer detections expanded the template catalog, which seeded matched-filter detection; the resulting event set was relocated to improve temporal and spatial resolution used to infer the sequence’s shallow fault geometry. The fault interpretation is author analysis from the denser catalog plus waveform and moment-tensor methods, not a model-generated classification alone.
